title: Analysis of serum haptoglobin fucosylation in hepatocellular carcinoma and liver cirrhosis of different etiologies.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a specific glycan modification (bifucosylated tetra‑antennary glycan on haptoglobin) that distinguishes HCC from cirrhosis and suggests diagnostic potential, meeting the biomarker criteria. However, quantitative performance data (e.g., AUC, sensitivity/specificity) are not provided, so the full text is needed to assess biomarker validity.

title: Asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI-CDG) initially mistaken for excessive alcohol consumption.

screening.reason: The abstract reports that elevated carbohydrate‑deficient transferrin (CDT), a glycan biomarker, is associated with asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI‑CDG), linking a glycan feature to a disease phenotype.

entities.evidence_sentence: The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.

title: Abundance-ratio-based semiquantitative analysis of site-specific N-linked glycopeptides present in the plasma of hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

screening.reason: The study identifies site‑specific N‑linked glycopeptides of vitronectin in plasma that differ between HCC patients and normal controls, indicating a glycan biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma. However, the abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics and sample size details, so the full text is needed to assess biomarker validity.

entities.evidence_sentence: Among these glycans, the abundance ratio of two representative glycoforms (fucosyl vs non-fucosyl) was significantly increased in HCC plasma relative to normal plasma.

title: Glycation of the complement regulatory protein CD59 is a novel biomarker for glucose handling in humans.

screening.reason: The abstract reports that glycated CD59 (a glycan modification) is quantitatively associated with HbA1c, OGTT response, and responds to insulin therapy in human subjects, directly linking a glycan-related biomarker to diabetes-related phenotypes.
